title: The affine-space trace is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings) on which $N$ is invertible. Work in the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the ordinary etale finite Tate sheaves of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]: $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$, their tensor powers $A_T(d)$, and $K(d)=K\otimes_A^LA_T(d)$. Let $d\geq0$ and let $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space], with compact-support direct image [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The explicit affine-space adjunction is the following one. For $d=1$, use the standard compactification $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^1_S$, $q:P\to S$, and compose $Dj_!\dashv j^*$ [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] with the projective-line adjunction of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], normalized by the trace $t_q$ of [def-amb-p1-trace]. For general $d$, let $F_d$ be the ordered composite of these affine-line compact-support functors in the coordinate tower, and form its composite adjunction using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; for $d=0$ use the identity adjunction. Its right adjoint is $G_d=p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$. On bounded-below inputs identify $F_d$ with $Rp_{d!}$ by the coherent compact-support composition isomorphisms [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Let
$$t_{p_d}:Rp_{d!}A_{\mathbf A^d_S}(d)[2d]\longrightarrow A_S$$
be the counit of $F_d\dashv G_d$ at $A_S$, with its source identified by this bounded-below comparison. Then $t_{p_d}$ is an isomorphism. For every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of Noetherian schemes, put $X'=\mathbf A^d_{S'}$, with projections $p'_d:X'\to S'$ and $g':X'\to\mathbf A^d_S$. Under the canonical Tate pullback identifications, and the compact-support exchange $C_{d,g}:g^*Rp_{d!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_{d!}g'^*$ of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] on the indicated bounded-below input, the actual maps satisfy
$$t_{p'_d}\circ C_{d,g,A(d)[2d]}=g^*t_{p_d}.$$
Thus the counit trace is compatible with arbitrary change of Noetherian base.

proof.text: For a Noetherian base $T$ with $N$ invertible put $U=\mathbf A^1_T$, $P=\mathbf P^1_T$, and $p=qj$. On the two standard charts $P$ is obtained from $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B[s]$, with $s=t^{-1}$, over every affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq T$. Take $U$ to be the first chart and take $i:T\hookrightarrow P$ to be $s=0$ in the second chart; hence $qi=1_T$ and $U=P\setminus i(T)$. The structural map $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. The affine-line projections are finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: the inverse image of every affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the single affine $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$, a quasi-compact scheme whose algebra is generated by $t$. Thus they are both locally of finite type and quasi-compact, so their sources, and inductively every base in the coordinate tower, are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Each affine-line projection is separated: over $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq T$ its relative diagonal is the closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}B[t_1,t_2]$ cut out by $t_1-t_2$, and these equations glue. This verifies the separatedness condition [def-weil-proper-morphism] required by compact-support composition and exchange. The open $j$ is quasi-compact: on the two standard affine charts its inverse images are respectively the whole chart and the principal open $D(s)$. Thus the displayed compactification also satisfies the quasi-compact-open condition in the exchange theorem. The invertibility of $N$ pulls back. These charts provide the chosen compactification, and [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Rp_!=Rq_*Dj_!$. For every $d$, [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] supplies the standard open $\mathbf A^d_T=D_+(T_0)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^d_T$ over $T$, and [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] makes its structural projection proper. On the standard chart $D_+(T_i)$ the inverse image of this open is the whole chart if $i=0$ and the principal open $D(T_0/T_i)$ otherwise, so it is quasi-compact. This supplies a compactification of each tower projection and of every composite $p_d$, as required by the composition and exchange statements in steps 7--9. Their finite-type and separatedness hypotheses also hold directly: over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ the inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}B[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ with its $d$ algebra generators, and the diagonal is cut out by $t_i-u_i$ for $1\leq i\leq d$. For $d=0$ these are the identity maps. The cited standard-open statement also justifies the chart compactification used above for $d=1$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: the standard affine-line compactification

proof.text:
Apply [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to the bounded-below complex $L=A_P(1)[2]$. Its maps are the open counit and the closed unit. Apply the triangulated functor $Rq_*$, using [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The closed immersion $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so $Ri_*=i_*$ on this bounded-below input by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]; the same assertion for constant-ring module sheaves follows by forgetting the action (the sheaf maps and exactness are unchanged). The derived direct-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], $qi=1_T$, and the Tate pullback identification [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identify the third vertex with $A_T(1)[2]$. We obtain a distinguished triangle
$$F_T\xrightarrow{a}Rq_*A_P(1)[2]\xrightarrow{r}A_T(1)[2]\longrightarrow F_T[1],\qquad F_T=Rp_!A_U(1)[2].$$
Here $a$ is $Rq_*$ of the open counit and $r$ is restriction to infinity.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: extension-by-zero triangle, twisted and shifted

proof.text: Use the specified decomposition $b_q:B_T\oplus A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*A_P(1)[2]$ from [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], where $B_T=A_T(1)[2]$. Restriction composed with the shifted twisted unit is $1_{B_T}$: under the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction this is the identity pulled back along $qi=1_T$. On the second component, restriction takes the Kummer boundary of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ to that of $i^*\mathcal O_P(1)$. Indeed pull back the transition functions and their local $N$th-root torsors in the defining Kummer boundary [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]; this is the boundary for the pulled-back line bundle. The second chart trivializes $\mathcal O_P(1)$ along $i(T)$, so this pulled-back bundle has the identity transition cocycle, whose boundary is zero. Consequently $rb_q=(1,0)$. By [def-amb-p1-trace], $t_qb_q=(0,1)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: restriction at infinity on the two summands

proof.text: Set $t_1=t_qa:F_T\to A_T$. In the long exact cohomology sequence of step 2, supplied by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], the map out of $H^n(B_T\oplus A_T)$ is the split projection to $H^n(B_T)$. It is surjective for every $n$, including $n-1$, so the preceding connecting map vanishes, and $H^n(a)$ identifies $H^n(F_T)$ with its kernel, namely the second summand $H^n(A_T)$. Since $t_q$ is projection to that summand, $H^n(t_1)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] makes this actual morphism $t_1$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: the restricted projective-line trace is an isomorphism

proof.text:
The adjunction $Dj_!\dashv j^*$ on ordinary derived categories is [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Compose it with the normalized adjunction $Rq_*\dashv q^*(-)(1)[2]$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. The composite counit, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], is
$$\epsilon_{p,K}=\epsilon_{q,K}\circ Rq_*(\epsilon_{j,q^*K(1)[2]}).$$
Its right adjoint is $j^*q^*(-)(1)[2]=p^*(-)(1)[2]$, using Tate pullback [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. At $K=A_T$, the projective counit is precisely $t_q$ (the inverse projection and tensor unit at the tensor unit are the unit constraints), and its preceding map is $a$. Thus the isomorphism proved in step 4 is the required counit, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, final sentence: identification of the actual composite counit

proof.text:
We need the same counit at a shifted Tate line $M=A_T(e)[2e]$, $e\geq0$. Here is the needed open projection comparison, without assuming a compact-support projection theorem. For a module sheaf $H$ on $U$ and the flat sheaf $V=A_P(e)$, adjunction gives a map $j_!(H\otimes_A j^*V)\to (j_!H)\otimes_A V$: its adjunct is the inverse of the open-unit identification $j^*((j_!H)\otimes V)=H\otimes j^*V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] its geometric stalks are that identity inside $U$ and $0\to0$ outside $U$; [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes it invertible; use its inverse as the open projection comparison. The flatness in [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] and exactness in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] allow this sheaf isomorphism to be applied termwise to complexes and shifted: tensor with $V$ already computes its derived tensor, and $Dj_!$ is termwise extension by zero. For clarity write $\alpha_{H,V}:j_!(H\otimes j^*V)\to j_!H\otimes V$ for the comparison before inversion. With $H=j^*L$, the two maps $(\epsilon_{j,L}\otimes1_V)\circ\alpha_{j^*L,V}$ and $\epsilon_{j,L\otimes V}$ have source $j_!(j^*L\otimes j^*V)$ and target $L\otimes V$, using the canonical restriction identification. Under $j_!\dashv j^*$, both adjuncts are $1_{j^*L\otimes j^*V}$ by the open unit-counit identity. Hence these maps are equal. This proves the counit square already on sheaves, and therefore termwise on complexes and in the derived categories. Identify $V=q^*A_T(e)$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Combine this comparison with the proper projection formula [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] for $q$. It gives
$$Rp_!(p^*M(1)[2])\cong M\otimes_A^L F_T.$$
To verify the proper part of the map comparison explicitly, put $L=A_P(1)[2]$, $J=Dj_!j^*L$, and $a=Rq_*(\epsilon_{j,L})$ as in step 2. Naturality of the stated canonical projection map in its second input gives
$$Rq_*(1_{q^*M}\otimes\epsilon_{j,L})\circ\pi_{q,M,J}=\pi_{q,M,L}\circ(1_M\otimes a).$$
Indeed the projection maps are adjuncts of tensoring the direct-image counit; the counit naturality square for $J\to L$ yields this equality after taking adjuncts. Together with the open counit square above, this identifies the preceding arrow under the displayed comparison with $1_M\otimes a$. The tensor symmetries and shifts used in these identifications contribute no sign, since the shifts are $2e$ and $2$. Under it the counit formula of step 5 becomes $1_M\otimes t_1$, followed by the tensor unit: the projective counit is explicitly $1_M\otimes t_q$ by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], and the preceding open counit is $1_M\otimes a$ by the commuting square just checked. This proves that $\epsilon_{p,M}$ is an isomorphism. The proper projection theorem applies since $A$ is finite, $q$ is proper and finite type, and $P$ is Noetherian; proper includes finite type, and step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] verify the latter. No general compact-support projection formula is being taken from a definition.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, first two sentences: projection formula on the chosen compactification

proof.text:
Induct on $d$, with induction claim that the specified tower counit at $A_S$ is invertible. At $d=0$, $p_0$ is the canonical identity [def-sbc-affine-space] and its counit is the identity [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The case $d=1$ is steps 2--5. For $d=e+1$ put $T=\mathbf A^e_S$, $r=p_e:T\to S$, $u:\mathbf A^1_T\to T$, so $p_d=ru$. The unbounded left functor of the formal composite adjunction is $F_d=F_eRu_!$. On bounded-below inputs [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] identifies it with $Rp_{d!}$, via $F_eRu_!\cong Rr_!Ru_!\cong Rp_{d!}$. For the counit at $A_S$, the input is a shifted Tate sheaf. Applying the innermost affine-line functor gives the next shifted Tate sheaf by step 6; repeating this checks boundedness at each intermediate stage before applying the comparison. The right adjoint of the composite, computed by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], is $u^*(r^*(-)(e)[2e])(1)[2]=p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$ by the tensor and pullback compatibilities of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Put $M=r^*A_S(e)[2e]=A_T(e)[2e]$. The actual counit at $A_S$ is
$$t_{p_d}=t_r\circ Rr_!(\epsilon_{u,M}).$$
Step 6 proves $\epsilon_{u,M}$ invertible, and the induction hypothesis proves $t_r$ invertible. A functor preserves inverses, and a composite of two invertible maps is invertible; this proves the induction claim for every $d$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: coordinate tower, identity base case, and composite counit

proof.text:
For arbitrary $g:T'\to T$ of Noetherian schemes use the pulled-back standard compactification. [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] supplies its canonical exchange; [def-cbc-exchange-map] defines it on this compactification as proper exchange followed by open extension exchange. The latter is [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. Denote it $C:g^*Rq_*Dj_!\to Rq'_*Dj'_!g_U^*$. The projective-line lemma [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] states compatibility of the actual normalized projective counits with proper exchange. Write $\beta_H:g_P^*Dj_!H\xrightarrow{\sim}Dj'_!g_U^*H$ for this exchange. Its inverse is the adjunction mate of the open unit as specified in [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change]. For $H=j^*L$, precompose both maps in the desired counit square with $\beta_H^{-1}$. They now have source $Dj'_!j'^*g_P^*L$ and target $g_P^*L$; each has adjunct $1_{j'^*g_P^*L}$ by the open unit-counit identity. Hence
$$g_P^*(\epsilon_{j,L})=\epsilon_{j',g_P^*L}\circ\beta_{j^*L}.$$
The degreewise equality descends to the derived categories, since these inverse-image and open-extension functors are exact. Applying $Rq'_*$ and pasting with projective exchange therefore gives, using the composite-counit formula,
$$\epsilon_{p',g^*K}\circ C_{G_pK}=g^*\epsilon_{p,K},\qquad G_pK=p^*K(1)[2],$$
with the canonical identification $g_U^*G_pK=G_{p'}g^*K$. More explicitly both sides factor through $Rq'_*g_P^*G_qK$, then through the pulled-back projective counit; the equality of their first arrows is exactly the open counit equality just checked. [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies these composites with the exchange of the composite adjunction. Tate pullback is canonical by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. This proves the desired equation for $d=1$, and also for the shifted Tate inputs $K=M$ used in step 7. We use this only on bounded-below inputs, as required by the compact-support exchange node.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, last sentence: base change through the explicit counits, affine-line case

proof.text:
Induct also on $d$ for the compatibility equation. It is the identity equation for $d=0$. For $d=e+1$ use $p_d=ru$ and $M=G_rA_S$ as in step 7, with their pulled-back towers. By the horizontal/vertical pasting and naturality of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], $C_{ru}$ is the composite of the exchanges for $r$ and $u$, and it commutes with application of $\epsilon_{u,M}$. The line equation from step 8 and naturality give
$$Rr'_!(\epsilon_{u',M'})\,C_{ru,G_uM}=C_{r,M}\,g^*Rr_!(\epsilon_{u,M}),\qquad M'=g_T^*M=G_{r'}A_{S'}.$$
Compose on the left with $t_{r'}$. The induction equation $t_{r'}C_{r,M}=g^*t_r$ turns the right side into $g^*(t_rRr_!(\epsilon_{u,M}))=g^*t_{p_d}$; the left side is $t_{p'_d}C_{ru,G_uM}$ by the composite-counit formula. Thus $t_{p'_d}C_{d,g}=g^*t_{p_d}$. The identifications $M'=G_{r'}A_{S'}$ and $G_uM=A(d)[2d]$ use precisely the composition-compatible finite Tate identifications [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Every term is a shifted sheaf after the preceding isomorphisms, so the bounded-below exchange and composition theorems apply at each stage. This proves compatibility for arbitrary Noetherian base changes without invoking smooth base change or smooth purity.
